reviewNote: Drafted by Claude from the chart for faculty review. Not validated teaching content.
summary: Lumpectomy with sentinel node biopsy booked as MAC for a very anxious 70 y who explicitly asked to be fully asleep; isosulfan blue will be injected (anaphylaxis risk, falsely low SpO2), she has severe PONV history, and the left arm is restricted.

asa.rationale: Paroxysmal AF on anticoagulation, HTN, hypothyroidism.

decision.rationale: Her stated preference is a reason to offer GA with LMA; MAC with deep sedation in a panicked patient is not safer. Apixaban held since 10/25 0800 (over 48 h).

redFlags.finding: Patient wants general anesthesia, MAC booked
redFlags.evidence: Patient message 10/05; PA reply deferred; tearful and repeatedly asking 'will I be asleep'.
redFlags.implication: Uncooperative patient under sedation and failure of informed consent.
redFlags.action: Discuss options; offer GA with LMA; document consent.

redFlags.implication: Anaphylaxis (about 1%), and falsely low SpO2 readings for some time.
redFlags.action: Expect SpO2 drop artifact; be ready for anaphylaxis with epinephrine.

redFlags.evidence: PONV after both GAs; hydrocodone intolerance; female nonsmoker.
Surgical side, IV in right hand.
redFlags.implication: No BP cuff or IV on left.
redFlags.action: Cuff on right arm or leg.

planItems.item: GA with LMA or MAC per discussion
Cefazolin 2 g within 60 min of incision
